handbookNote: Washington Boating Program handbook (Boat-Ed/Kalkomey, 2018, content approved by Washington State Parks Boating Programs) -- Washington has no single official state-administered boating exam; its 2005/2008 boater education law requires operators 12+ years old, born on or after January 1, 1955, to hold a Washington Boater Education Card to operate a motorboat of 15+ horsepower (age 14+ to operate a PWC; illegal to rent/lease a PWC to anyone under 16), obtained by taking a State Parks-approved course (classroom, online, or home-study) and passing that course's own exam, then applying for the $10 card (never expires; an equivalency exam option exists for experienced boaters) -- in practice this means the NASBLA-approved course vendor's own quiz IS the de facto test, not a separate state exam; Boat-Ed's official Washington course (boat-ed.com/washington, the vendor State Parks' own handbook cross-references) confirms live 2026 a 70% passing score on unit quizzes and 80% on the final exam with unlimited retake attempts, while BoatUS Foundation's Washington course (boatus.org/washington) separately advertises 60 final exam questions -- this 60q/80% convergence matches this project's CA/FL/PA/GA boating precedent -- price matches this project's Motorcycle-tier boating convention ($7.99), not a placeholder
